name: v1_baseline
description: Reference model: HalfNormal(0.3) solar prior, StudentT likelihood, polynomial temperature. Anchor for all comparisons.

name: v2_strict_solar
description: Sceptical solar prior: Exponential(lam=2) places most mass near zero. Tests whether data overcomes a strongly regularising prior on eta.

name: v3_normal_likelihood
description: Normal likelihood: removes heavy tails. Quantifies the robustness cost of not down-weighting blackout and macroeconomic shock days.

name: v4_lognormal_solar
description: LogNormal(mu=-1, sigma=0.8) solar prior: centred near REE-implied eta ~0.37. Tests a log-symmetric, physically anchored prior.

name: v5_heavy_tail_solar
description: HalfCauchy(0.5) solar prior: very heavy tails. Tests whether the data constrains eta from above even under an essentially flat prior.

name: v6_wide_solar_only
description: Wide HalfNormal(5) on solar prior only, all other priors unchanged. Isolates the effect of solar prior width from other hyperparameter choices.

name: v7_piecewise
description: Piecewise HDD/CDD baseline. Replaces the polynomial with separate Heating Degree Day and Cooling Degree Day terms (thresholds 18C/22C). Follows Engle et al. (1986) and Bessec & Fouquau (2008), who showed piecewise temperature outperforms polynomials for European electricity demand. HalfNormal priors enforce both coefficients are positive (demand rises away from the comfort band).

name: v8_autoregressive
description: Autoregressive baseline: adds 7-day lagged demand as a predictor (rho_lag ~ N(0.8, 0.2)). Follows Elamin & Fukushima (2018) short-term load forecasting literature. NOTE: excluded from the main LOO leaderboard because lag-7 demand absorbs autocorrelation rather than physical drivers, inflating ELPD by ~2300 points spuriously. Run separately to quantify the autocorrelation effect.

name: v9_thi
description: Temperature-Humidity Index (THI) baseline. Replaces raw temperature with THI = T - 0.55*(1 - RH/100)*(T - 14.5), which adjusts for perceived heat stress. Follows Valor et al. (2001) and Mirasgedis et al. (2007), who showed THI outperforms raw temperature for Spanish and Mediterranean electricity demand modelling.
